about: Start a game's gallery, sports (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-redo.md Round 2): every game type a sport's fans already know, per sport family, named the way they say it, each with an engine spec our check passes on the sport's page (scripts/dev-test/sport-gallery-check.js) or `coming` with the step or engine piece that would bring it. Read by sports.js (its header says how a spec, a `by` and a `len` resolve). One game type can be the same engine spec as another: the gallery repeats itself where the engine isn't one to one. `spec` is a whole spec, or { standard, with }: one of the sport's standard games (src/lib/sports/defaults, as defaultsFor gives them: a league's own over the sport's, football's lineup slots) with `with`'s parts over it, one level deep. `by` keys a family ("soccer") or a league ("football/college-football"): its words, spec or coming over the base's, the league's last. `on`: the pages it's made for (pages, below). `lens`: its length on another page. `needs`: something the page has to supply (keepers: last season's game, PageFacts.lastSeason). `gap`: the fuller reason behind a `coming`.

bases.name: Head-to-head points
bases.plain: Draft a team; face a friend each week
bases.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week your starters' points face one of the couch's teams, and the most wins takes the season.

football.name: Fantasy football
football.plain: Draft a team; face a friend each week
football.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup by position: a quarterback, two running backs, two receivers, a tight end, a flex, a kicker and a defense. Each week your starters' points face one of the couch's teams, and the most wins takes the season.

soccer.name: Draft league
soccer.plain: FPL-style: draft a squad, face a friend
soccer.about: Draft a squad of 15 and start 11 each round, scored the way Fantasy Premier League scores. Each round your points face one of the couch's teams.

bases.name: Season points
bases.plain: Most points all season wins
bases.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup, with no matchups. Every point your starters score adds up, and the most at the end wins.

bases.name: Best ball
bases.plain: Draft once; your best count by themselves
bases.about: Draft a full roster once and never set a lineup. Each game your best players' points count for you on their own.

bases.name: Head-to-head categories
bases.plain: Win more stat columns than a friend
bases.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week you face one of the couch across the standard categories, and every category you win counts as a win.

basketball.name: 9-cat head to head
basketball.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week you face one of the couch across nine categories (points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, threes, both shooting percentages and turnovers), and every category you win counts as a win.

baseball.name: 5x5 head to head
baseball.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week you face one of the couch across the 5x5: runs, homers, RBI, steals and average for your hitters; wins, saves, strikeouts, ERA and WHIP for your pitchers. Every category you win counts as a win.

hockey.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week you face one of the couch across ten categories, six for skaters and four for goalies, and every category you win counts as a win.

bases.name: Roto
bases.plain: Ranked in every stat, all season
bases.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Every category ranks the whole couch over the season, and your places add up: the most points from them wins.

bases.name: Guillotine league
bases.plain: Lowest score each week is out
bases.about: Draft a team and set your lineup. Each week the lowest score is cut and their players go back up for grabs; the last team standing wins.

bases.name: Keeper league
bases.plain: Keep two from last season's team
bases.about: Keep two players from your team in this couch's game last season, each costing one of your earliest draft rounds, then draft the rest. Then face one of the couch each week.
bases.needs: your couch's game on last season

bases.name: Dynasty league
bases.plain: Keep your whole team, year after year
bases.about: Your roster is yours for good: keep everyone each year and add the new players in a rookie draft.
bases.coming: No step yet: a rookie draft
bases.gap: Keepers keep up to a whole team across seasons (A10 part 4's get.keep), but nothing drafts only the year's new players: a roster doesn't say who's a rookie, so no pool can be just them.

bases.name: Auction draft
bases.plain: Bid for your team, 200 to spend
bases.about: Everyone has 200 to bid, in private, on the players they want, and the highest bid gets each one. Then set your lineup and face one of the couch each week.

bases.name: Salary cap
bases.plain: Daily-fantasy style: fit a team under a cap
bases.about: Every player has a price; build a team under the cap for the night or the week. Two of you can have the same player.
bases.coming: No step yet: a price for each player
bases.gap: A salary cap prices each castaway by their points so far in a draft scored by moments (A10 part 3b); a sport's stats price nobody, so the cap has nothing to cost (our check: "A salary cap's prices are each castaway's points so far by the game's rules: a draft scored by moments").

bases.name: One-week draft
bases.plain: Draft 3 players for this week only
bases.about: Everyone drafts three players for this week's games, and every one of them scores. Most points when the week's games are over wins.

soccer.name: One-round draft
soccer.plain: Draft 3 players for this round only
soccer.about: Everyone drafts three players for this round's matches, and every one of them scores. Most points when the round is over wins.

bases.name: Game-night draft
bases.plain: 3 players each, one game
bases.about: Like daily fantasy without the salaries: everyone drafts three players from the two teams, and every one of them scores. Most points at the final whistle wins.

baseball.about: Like daily fantasy without the salaries: everyone drafts three players from the two teams, and every one of them scores. Most points after the last out wins.

basketball.about: Like daily fantasy without the salaries: everyone drafts three players from the two teams, and every one of them scores. Most points at the final buzzer wins.

hockey.about: Like daily fantasy without the salaries: everyone drafts three players from the two teams, and every one of them scores. Most points at the final horn wins.

bases.name: Playoff fantasy
bases.plain: Draft 8 for the whole playoffs
bases.about: Before the playoffs start, everyone drafts eight players, and every one of them scores in every playoff game they play. Players on teams that go deep score the most.

bases.name: Pick'em
bases.plain: Pick the winner of every game
bases.about: Each week, pick the winner of every game before it starts; each pick locks at its own game's start. A point for every one right, and the most points wins.

soccer.plain: Win, lose or draw: every match
soccer.about: Each round, call every match before it kicks off: either side, or a draw. A point for every one right, and the most points wins.

bases.name: Pick'em
bases.plain: Who wins each of their games
bases.about: Before each of their games, pick who wins. A point for every one right (a tie counts for nobody), and the most points wins.

soccer.plain: Win, lose or draw, each match
soccer.about: Before each of their matches, call it: either side, or a draw. A point for every one right, and the most points wins.

bases.name: Confidence pool
bases.plain: Rank your picks, surest first
bases.about: Pick the winner of every game, then rank your picks by how sure you are: your surest is worth the most. A right pick scores its rank, and the most points wins.

ask.ask: Who wins? Rank your picks, surest first

football/college-football.about: Pick the winner of every game, bowl season included, then rank your picks by how sure you are: your surest is worth the most. A right pick scores its rank, and the most points wins.

bases.name: Head-to-head pick'em
bases.plain: Your picks against a friend's each week
bases.about: Pick the winner of every game each week, and face one of the couch: whoever gets more right wins the week. The most wins takes the season.

ask.ask: Who wins, or is it a draw?

bases.name: Against the spread
bases.plain: Pick every game with the points
bases.about: Pick every game against the betting line: the favourite has to win by more than the spread. A point for every one right.
bases.coming: No step yet: each game's spread
bases.gap: The engine keeps each game's over/under line as its pick opens (L3 part 3b, line 'game'), never its spread, though ESPN's odds have one; and a side is graded by who won outright.

bases.name: Survivor pool
bases.plain: Pick one team to win; never the same twice
bases.about: Each week, pick one team to win. Right, you're through; wrong, you're out. You can't use a team twice, and the last one standing wins.
bases.coming: No step yet: one team a week from the slate
bases.gap: A pool's picks are players (get.by 'pick', repeat 'never'), and a pick of a side is one game's: each: 'game' asks every game of the week. Nothing picks one team from all of the week's games, never the same twice. (Our check passes a lone side question on a slate, but the grader keeps no single game for a slate's week, so it would never count.)

soccer.name: Last man standing
soccer.about: Each round, pick one team to win. Right, you're through; a draw or a loss and you're out. You can't use a team twice, and the last one standing wins.

bases.name: Pick a few
bases.plain: Pick 3: who has the most?
bases.about: Before each of their games, pick three players. Three points for each one who leads the game in the stat, and the most points wins.

football.plain: Pick 3: who gets the most receiving yards?
football.about: Before each of their games, pick three players. Three points if one of them has the most receiving yards in the game, and the most points wins.

basketball.about: Before each of their games, pick three players. Three points if one of them is the game's top scorer, and the most points wins.

baseball.plain: Pick 3: who gets the most total bases?
baseball.about: Before each of their games, pick three players. Three points if one of them has the most total bases in the game, and the most points wins.

hockey.plain: Pick 3: who gets the most points?
hockey.about: Before each of their games, pick three players. Three points if one of them has the most points (goals and assists) in the game, and the most points wins.

soccer.about: Before each of their matches, pick three players. Three points if one of them scores the most goals in it, and the most points wins.

bases.name: Scorer pool
bases.plain: Pick 3; a point for every score
bases.about: Everyone picks three players in private, and two of you can pick the same one. A point for every time one of yours scores, and the most points wins.

football.name: Touchdown pool
football.plain: Pick 3; a point for every touchdown
football.about: Everyone picks three players in private, and two of you can pick the same one. A point for every rushing or receiving touchdown they score, and the most points wins.

baseball.name: Homer pick
baseball.plain: Pick 3 hitters; a point for every homer
baseball.about: Everyone picks three hitters in private, and two of you can pick the same one. A point for every home run they hit, and the most points wins.

hockey.name: Goal pool
hockey.plain: Pick 3; a point for every goal

soccer.name: Goalscorer pool
soccer.plain: Pick 3; a point for every goal

bases.name: Home run pool
bases.plain: Pick 8 hitters; most homers all season
bases.about: Everyone picks eight hitters before the season, in private, and two of you can pick the same one. Every home run they hit counts, and the most at the end wins.

bases.name: Beat the Streak
bases.plain: Pick a hitter a day; keep the hits coming
bases.about: Each day, pick one hitter. A hit keeps your streak alive; a hitless day ends it. The longest streak wins.
bases.coming: No step yet: a pick scored by a stat
bases.gap: A pick each day scored by a sport's stats has no place yet (our check: "a pick each episode scored by its stats has no place yet: a draft's lineup or best ball does"); a pool's pick survives by staying in or by moments, and nothing reads a sport's stats for a pick.

bases.name: Prop sheet
bases.plain: Winner, top player, the total
bases.about: Three calls before each of their games: who wins, who leads the game in the big stat, and is the total over or under the line. A point for each right.

football.about: Three calls before each of their games: who wins, who throws for the most yards, and are the total points over or under the line. A point for each right; the Super Bowl's party sheet.

ask.ask: Who throws for the most yards?

basketball.about: Three calls before each of their games: who wins, who scores the most, and are the total points over or under the line. A point for each right.

baseball.about: Three calls before each of their games: who wins, who gets the most hits, and are the total runs over or under the line. A point for each right.

hockey.about: Three calls before each of their games: who wins, who gets the most points, and are the total goals over or under the line. A point for each right.

soccer.about: Three calls before each of their matches: the result (a draw counts), who scores the most, and are the total goals over or under the line. A point for each right.

ask.ask: Who wins, or is it a draw?

bases.name: Over / under
bases.plain: Over or under the line?
bases.about: Before each of their games, call the total over or under the sportsbook's line, kept from when the pick opens. A point for each right.

bases.name: Over/under pick'em
bases.plain: Over or under, every game
bases.about: Each week, call every game's total over or under its own line, each kept from when its pick opens. A point for every one right.

bases.name: Winner and margin
bases.plain: Who wins, and by how much?
bases.about: Before each of their games, pick the winner and guess the margin. A point for the winner, and a point for whoever's closest on the margin.

bases.name: Score predictor
bases.plain: Call the exact final score
bases.about: Before each game, call the final score. Points for the right result, more for the exact score.
bases.coming: No step yet: each side's own score as an answer
bases.gap: A game's final settles who won, the total or the margin (answers.js standingIn), never each side's score; two numbers (total and margin) can't say an exact score either.

bases.name: First scorer
bases.plain: Who scores first?
bases.about: Before each game, pick who scores first. Points if you're right.
bases.coming: No step yet: the order of a game's plays
bases.gap: Who scored first needs the order of a game's plays; the engine keeps each game's box score (its counts), not its plays, and a stat's settle takes the most, the least or a value.

bases.name: Squares
bases.plain: A grid of the scores' last digits
bases.about: Take squares on a 10-by-10 grid; the digits are drawn once everyone has theirs. When a quarter ends, the square matching the two scores' last digits wins.

basketball/mens-college-basketball.about: Take squares on a 10-by-10 grid; the digits are drawn once everyone has theirs. At halftime and at the final, the square matching the two scores' last digits wins.

bases.name: Betting pool
bases.plain: Bet points on the total, the margin, the top player
bases.about: Everyone starts with 500 points to bet on each of their games: the total over or under the line, the margin, and who leads the game in the big stat, or a ticket of them. Points, never money.

ask.ask: Who throws for the most yards?

bases.plain: Both calls right: triple
bases.about: Before each of their games, call the total over or under the line and who leads the game in the big stat. Get both right and your points triple.

ask.ask: Who throws for the most yards?

bases.plain: Pick every round to the title

football.about: Before the playoffs start, pick who wins every game, round by round to the Super Bowl. A point for each right in the first round, doubling every round after.

bases.name: Weekly high score
bases.plain: Top score each week wins the week
bases.about: Draft a full roster and set your lineup. Each week's top score wins the week, and the most weeks won takes the season.

soccer.plain: Top score each round wins the round

bases.name: Live calls
bases.plain: Guess each play as it happens
bases.about: Call what happens next while the game is on: the next drive, the next at-bat, the next goal. The earlier you call it, the more it pays.

bases.name: Season league
bases.plain: Draft a stable; start some each event
bases.about: Draft a stable before the season and choose who starts each event. Everyone you start scores what they do, and the most points over the season wins.

golf.name: Season of tournaments
golf.about: Draft eight golfers before the season and start six each tournament: birdies, bogey-free rounds and the finish all score. The most points over the season wins.

racing.plain: Draft drivers; start some each race
racing.about: Draft a stable of drivers before the season and start most of them each race: the finish, laps led and fastest laps score. The most points over the season wins.

mma.name: Season of cards
mma.about: Draft eight fighters and start six each card; each starter scores on the nights they fight, for strikes, takedowns and the way they win. The most points over the season wins.

tennis.about: Draft eight players and start six each tournament; every match they play scores, games and sets won included. The most points over the season wins.

bases.name: Tournament draft
bases.plain: A few each, one event

golf.about: Everyone drafts three golfers for this tournament, and every hole they play scores. The most points after Sunday wins.

racing.name: Race-day draft

mma.name: Fight-night draft

tennis.about: Everyone drafts three players for this tournament, and every match they play scores. The most points after the final wins.

golf.about: Before each tournament, pick the winner. Five points if you're right, and the most points over the season wins.

racing.about: Before each race weekend, pick the winner. Five points if you're right, and the most points over the season wins.

mma.name: Main event pick

tennis.name: Pick the champion
